1.grade_fit_note: Map scale is familiar grade-5 content and the sentence defines the meaning outright ('one inch stands for ten miles').
1.note: The context clue is close to a definition, so the item is easier than its target; 'series of notes' (musical scale) has no pull in a map sentence.

2.grade_fit_note: Pronoun case in a compound object is standard grade-6 content (L.6.1a).
2.note: A clean 2x2 grid; 'him and I' is the classic hypercorrection lure.
dimensions_varied: case of first pronoun (subjective he / objective him)
case of second pronoun (subjective I / objective me)

3.grade_fit_note: Past perfect with 'by the time' fits grade 5 (L.5.1b-c).
3.note: 'By the time ... reached' needs the past perfect; C and D are clear tense mismatches, B is the realistic lure.
dimensions_varied: auxiliary form (had / has / will have / is)

4.grade_fit_note: The stem names 'great force', and only one option carries that meaning, so no style judgment is needed.
4.free_elimination: A, B and D: the stem asks for 'great force', and 'crashed' is the only option that means force, so the others go without reading the passage.
4.note: Options differ along the axis the stem names: the stem gives away the key. 'Fallen' is the only real competitor.

5.grade_fit_note: Cause-and-effect transitions fit grade 5, though the effect is spelled out plainly.
5.note: 'For example' is weak because sentence 3 is not an instance of anything; 'However' is the only real contrast lure.

6.grade_fit_note: An introductory-clause comma plus a plural-vs-possessive apostrophe fit grade 5.
6.note: A 2x2 on comma and apostrophe; both errors are common student errors.

7.grade_fit_note: Agreement with 'each' plus agreement in a 'there are' inversion is solid grade-6 work.
7.note: Two independent agreement decisions in a 2x2; 'were' after 'drawings' is the attraction lure.
dimensions_varied: number of first verb (singular was / plural were)
number of second verb (plural are / singular is)

8.grade_fit_note: An irregular plural possessive and the semicolon before a conjunctive adverb suit grade 7.
8.note: A 2x2 of possessive and comma splice; both lures are attractive.

9.grade_fit_note: A direct-address comma and a comma before the conjunction are grade-5/6 skills.
9.note: Direct-address commas are a grade-5 standard (L.5.2c), so this sits a little below the target; D has both errors.

10.grade_fit_note: An adverb with an action verb against an adjective after a linking verb suits grade 7.
10.note: 'Smelled deliciously' is the strong hypercorrection lure; the 2x2 structure is clean.
dimensions_varied: first slot: adverb vs adjective (cautiously / cautious)
second slot: adjective vs adverb (delicious / deliciously)

11.grade_fit_note: 'Especially' is a common grade-5 spelling demand.
11.note: Misspellings vary on the x/s substitution and the single l; 'expecialy' stacks both errors and has little pull.

12.grade_fit_note: Misplaced and dangling modifiers are grade-7 content (L.7.1c).
12.note: B (brother covered) and C (dangling: Leah covered) are classic errors; A is grammatical but says Leah is covered, so it also fails.
dimensions_varied: position of the participial phrase (after subject / sentence-final after indirect object / sentence-initial / directly after the noun it modifies)
comma setoff (parenthetical commas / none / introductory comma)

13.grade_fit_note: Using context to choose the less common sense of a multiple-meaning word fits grade 6.
13.note: 'Something no class at our school had tried before' pins the meaning; C (book sense) and A (fiction) are good lures.

14.grade_fit_note: 'Tempered' in its 'moderated' sense with a clear context clue suits grade 7.
14.note: 'Nobody left feeling discouraged' supports softened; D (tempered steel) and A (heat) are strong lures from other senses.

15.grade_fit_note: Correlative conjunctions are a grade-5 standard (L.5.1e).
15.note: 'Decide which one' rules out neither/nor; the mixed pairs B and C are ungrammatical, and C has little pull.

16.grade_fit_note: Region vs direction capitalization is learnable earlier, but grade 7 is still reasonable.
16.note: A 2x2 on Southwest (region) vs north (direction); slightly easy for its band.

17.grade_fit_note: Inferring a theme from the narrator's change of heart fits grade 6.
17.note: The tape, 'I promised cookies' and the 48 count support D; B has some support since the flat cookies sold, but nothing was 'better', so it is a strong near-miss.

18.grade_fit_note: Inferring a character's motive from later action is grade-6 work, but the evidence here is thin.
18.note: The key depends on reading the later tape back onto the doorway moment; D (she offered help and was refused) is equally defensible at that point in the story, so the key is weak.

19.grade_fit_note: Reading the narrator's view from her dialogue suits grade 6.
19.note: 'I promised cookies. Not crumbs in a bag.' supports B directly; nothing suggests A.

20.grade_fit_note: 'Set myself a goal' is a common idiom, and 'established' is easy to pick out.
20.note: D (hardened) borrows from the butter detail and is the only real lure.

21.grade_fit_note: Author's-purpose questions on a key line of dialogue suit grade 6.
21.note: The key paraphrases the quote ('what we needed') almost word for word, which makes it easy to match; C is false because the cookies were never broken.

22.grade_fit_note: Season vs nationality capitalization is a basic grade-5 skill.
22.note: A 2x2 on Summer and Korean; a straightforward item.

23.grade_fit_note: 'Qualified' in its 'limited/restricted' sense is a demanding grade-7 word with a usable context clue.
23.note: 'Results could change' supports limited; A (certified) is the strong familiar-sense lure, and D (described) has some pull.

24.grade_fit_note: Capitalizing a proper noun and the continuation of a split quotation suit grade 7, though slightly easy.
24.note: A 2x2 on Museum and the interrupted-quote 'is'.

25.grade_fit_note: 'Privilege' is a classic grade-7 spelling demon.
25.note: All three misspellings are realistic ('priviledge' especially).

26.note: A 2x2 on doubled m and dropped e; D stacks both errors.

27.grade_fit_note: The 'keep a holiday' sense of observe, with a strong context clue, fits grade 6.
27.note: 'Holding a parade' points to celebrates; C (watches) is the familiar-sense lure, and A (obeys, as in observing rules) is plausible to students.

28.grade_fit_note: A common noun for a relative after 'my' and title capitalization suit grade 6.
28.note: A 2x2 on grandmother and the article 'the' in a title.

29.grade_fit_note: 'Yield' as produce, with a strong clue ('twice as many tomatoes'), fits grade 5.
29.note: A (surrender) and C (yield sign) are good lures from other senses; B has little pull.

30.grade_fit_note: Separating the decisive cause from the other contributing causes is solid grade-7 central-idea work.
30.note: The passage rules out A (members kept putting off a vote) and B (council made no change after the flood) in so many words; D is minor. Four parallel 'X won the council over' options, varied only by agent, are a clean design.

31.grade_fit_note: 'Raised the idea' is a common collocation, and the item is easy for grade 7.
31.note: C (collected, from the fundraising) and D (lifted) are lures; context makes 'mentioned' obvious.

32.grade_fit_note: The key is stated almost word for word ('the ferry had become too risky to run in high water'), so no inference is needed.
32.note: An 'inference' item answered by retrieval; A is defensible as an inference about Otto before April (he 'changed his mind' and said his living mattered less), so the key is not exclusive.

33.grade_fit_note: Telling apart what changed Otto's mind and what moved the council suits grade 7.
33.note: B is the strong lure, but paragraph 5 says the flood changed nothing for the council; D is wrong on chronology.

34.grade_fit_note: The answer is stated outright in paragraph 2 ('saw the bridge as a threat to the ferryman's living').
34.note: A literal retrieval item; the key's wording also matches item 32's option A word for word, so the set repeats phrasing across items.
